brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.evidence: Seven full hex bases at level 0 forming a flower: centre piece (0,0) plus six around it at (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0). check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Seven full covers on the top face of every cell (cover:-1,0,0 through cover:1,0,0), one per base.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid end caps on the exposed outside faces of the perimeter cells; lockJoints added 12 joint bolts.

finish.summary: Built a flat seven-cell hex work surface: one centre base with six surrounding bases, all covered on top, with 18 end caps closing the open outside edges and joints bolted. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Note: plan_build stacked pieces vertically instead of laying them out flat; I undid that and placed the bases from the offered sockets. No props were added since the brief did not call for any.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
